messages:
Sam: Quick proposal thread — thinking about a mixed-capacity pool approach per region: keep a small on-demand floor for steady load + a separate spot/preemptible burst pool. Goal: 30-40% cost savings while keeping tail latency SLOs.
Devon: +1. Key questions: how big should the on-demand floor be? How do we handle eviction storms and slow restarts that blow up latency?
Ana: If we're doing a floor, it needs to be per-AZ or per-region? Cross-AZ networking cost and startup time differ a lot. I lean region-level floor with AZ-aware placement for redundancy.
Mike: We should quantify steady-state GPU usage from last 90 days per region. My quick calc: us-west1 120 avg GPUs, p95 200. If we set floor=40% of p95 we get ~80 on-demand, rest spot.
Sara: Also think about burst pool capacity caps so we don’t accidentally flood spot markets in one region and cause more evictions elsewhere. Add backoff/slow-start to burst scaling.
autoscaler-bot: [info] Recent trend: preemptions in europe-west4 increased 2.3x this week (gcp). Recommend increasing checkpoint frequency for long-running jobs.
Devon: Eviction handling: two-pronged plan
- Short jobs (<30s) run on spot only
- Medium jobs checkpoint async and can restart on spot or on-demand
- Latency-sensitive inference routed to on-demand pool or pinned instances
Ana: For checkpointing, we need a fast warm-start path for models: keep VMs with preloaded containers in a warm pool. That reduces cold-start from ~45s to ~7s.
Mike: Example autoscaler snippet I prototyped:
```yaml
policy:
  region: us-west1
  pools:
    - name: on-demand-floor
      min_size: 80
      instance_type: a100
      preemptible: false
    - name: spot-burst
      min_size: 0
      max_size: 400
      instance_type: a100-spot
      preemptible: true
  scaling:
    burst_backoff_seconds: 120
    cooldown: 60
    eviction_threshold: 0.15
``` 
Sam: Love that. Couple additions: an admission controller that routes requests by latency budget and a probation window for spot-backed replicas (e.g., must survive N minutes before eligible for production traffic).
Sara: Can we add a cap on spot-to-on-demand failover rate? If too many failovers per minute, switch to rejecting new low-priority jobs rather than promoting to on-demand and blowing our floor.
Devon: Cost model: assume spot rate = 0.35 * on-demand. With floor 40% of peak and 60% spot burst, rough cost = 0.4*1.0 + 0.6*0.35 = 0.61 => ~39% savings vs all on-demand. But this ignores extra warm-pool overhead (~5-7% infra cost).
Ana: Network/placement nuance: if warm-pool lives in different AZ than spot, the model load might cross AZs — need affinity and routing rules.
Sam: Operational checks we should add to console/alerts:
- Spot eviction rate per minute > 0.1 => alert
- Failover promotions per minute > X => alert & autoscaler throttling
- Warm-pool health < 90% => don't scale spot fast
Mike: For rollout, propose 2-week canary in us-west1 with floor=50% of p95 and conservative burst caps, then expand to eu if stable.
Sara: +1. Who owns canary metrics? Suggest infra/sre pair to monitor latency SLO, cost delta, and evictions.
Devon: I'll draft the RFC today with config defaults and rollback thresholds. Also adding a short checklist for product teams about workload readiness for spot (stateless vs stateful, checkpointing).
Sam: Perfect. Please link RFC here when ready; I'll shepherd review. :thumbsup:
